source.original_text:
The increment of the actual completed Itô process between two deterministic times is in L². Its squared expectation equals the probability-time energy of the original integrand on that cell.

The progressive real integrand belongs to the probability-time L² domain.
The driver is scalar Brownian relative to a filtration satisfying the usual conditions, with finite sample measure and a positive construction horizon T.
The deterministic times satisfy s≤t≤T; the interval may be empty.

\mathbb E[(I_t-I_s)^2]=\int_{\Omega\times[s,t)}|\eta(\omega,u)|^2\,d(\mu\otimes du|_{[0,T]}).

theorem anonymous_target.{u_1}
  {Omega : Type u_1} {m : MeasurableSpace Omega} {filtration : MeasureTheory.Filtration NNReal m}
  {mu : MeasureTheory.Measure Omega} [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure mu] {T : NNReal} {B : NNReal → Omega → ℝ}
  (eta : AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ProgressiveL2.ProgressiveL2Integrand filtration mu T)
  (hT : 0 < T)
  (hB :
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.BrownianMotion.IsBrownianMotionWithFiltration B filtration
      mu)
  (hUsual : AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ProgressiveL2.SatisfiesUsualConditions filtration mu)
  {s t : NNReal} (hst : s ≤ t) (htT : t ≤ T) :
  have increment := fun omega =>
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoIntegralProcess.itoIntegralProcess eta hT hB hUsual t
        omega -
      AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoIntegralProcess.itoIntegralProcess eta hT hB hUsual s
        omega;
  MeasureTheory.MemLp increment 2 mu ∧
    ∫ (omega : Omega), increment omega ^ 2 ∂mu =
      ∫ (z : Omega × NNReal) in Prod.snd ⁻¹' Set.Ico s t,
        AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ProgressiveL2.processFunction eta.process z ^
          2 ∂AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ElementaryItoIntegral.processTimeMeasure mu T

blind_reconstruction.text:
Measurable Omega with finite measure mu and filtration F; scalar Brownian process B; scalar progressive L² integrand eta; its completed Ito integral I. Two ordered times and the integral increment.

T>0 is nonnegative real. B,eta,I:[0,infinity)×Omega→R. lambda_T is Lebesgue measure on [0,T] represented on nonnegative reals; product measure is mu⊗lambda_T. s,t∈[0,infinity), s≤t≤T.

Assumptions: eta is strongly progressive for F and (omega,r)↦eta(r,omega) is in L²(mu⊗lambda_T). B satisfies standard scalar Brownian finite-dimensional distributions: for every finite nonnegative time set S, (B_s)_{s∈S} has centered Gaussian law with covariance (s,t)↦min(s,t), and B has continuous paths mu-a.e. In particular B_0=0 is required almost surely, not for every sample, is strongly adapted to F, and B_t-B_s is independent of F_s for every s≤t. F is right-continuous and every subset S⊆Omega with mu(S)=0 belongs to F_t for every t≥0. s≤t and t≤T.

Conclusion: I is the specified continuous completed Ito integral of eta against B: the canonical elementary-integral limit off its null uniform-Cauchy exceptional set, zero on that set, and constant after T. Let D(omega)=I(t,omega)-I(s,omega). Then D∈L²(mu) and ∫D²dmu=∫_{Omega×[s,t)}eta(v,omega)²d(mu⊗lambda_T)(omega,v).

Quantifier order: For every filtered finite measure setup, eta and Brownian B satisfying assumptions, and every pair s≤t≤T, the increment is in L² and its second moment has the stated value.

Scope: Exact second-moment identity for one increment on the fixed finite horizon. Time restriction is [s,t), and s=t is allowed.

Constant dependencies: No existential constants or rates.

import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoIntegralProcess

/-! # Cellwise isometry for the completed Itô process -/

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoIntegralIncrement

open Filter MeasureTheory Set
open scoped NNReal
open BrownianMotion ProgressiveL2 ElementaryItoIntegral ItoIntegralProcess
  ItoTerminalCompletion ElementaryItoL2

/-- A deterministic-cell increment of the completed Itô process has squared
expectation equal to the probability-time energy on that cell. -/
theorem itoIntegralProcess_increment_isometry
    {Omega : Type*} {m : MeasurableSpace Omega}
    {filtration : Filtration ℝ≥0 m} {mu : Measure Omega} [IsFiniteMeasure mu]
    {T : ℝ≥0} {B : ℝ≥0 → Omega → ℝ}
    (eta : ProgressiveL2Integrand filtration mu T) (hT : 0 < T)
    (hB : IsBrownianMotionWithFiltration B filtration mu)
    (hUsual : SatisfiesUsualConditions filtration mu)
    {s t : ℝ≥0} (hst : s ≤ t) (htT : t ≤ T) :
    let increment := fun omega =>
      itoIntegralProcess eta hT hB hUsual t omega - itoIntegralProcess eta hT hB hUsual s omega
    MemLp increment 2 mu ∧
      (∫ omega, (increment omega)^2 ∂mu) =
        ∫ z in Prod.snd ⁻¹' Set.Ico s t,
          (processFunction eta.process z)^2 ∂(processTimeMeasure mu T) := by
  intro increment
  let right := eta.restrictAt t
  let left := eta.restrictAt s
  let difference := ProgressiveL2Algebra.sub right left
  let L := itoIntegralTerminal difference hT hB
  have hL : L = itoIntegralTerminal right hT hB - itoIntegralTerminal left hT hB :=
    itoIntegralTerminal_sub right left hT hB
  have hCoe := Lp.coeFn_sub (itoIntegralTerminal right hT hB) (itoIntegralTerminal left hT hB)
  have hInc : increment =ᵐ[mu] fun omega => L omega := by
    rw [hL]
    filter_upwards [itoIntegralProcess_at_eq_terminal eta hT hB hUsual htT,
      itoIntegralProcess_at_eq_terminal eta hT hB hUsual (hst.trans htT),hCoe] with omega hRt hLt hSub
    exact (congrArg₂ (· - ·) hRt hLt).trans hSub.symm
  refine ⟨(memLp_congr_ae hInc).2 (Lp.memLp L), ?_⟩
  let cell : Set (Omega × ℝ≥0) := Prod.snd ⁻¹' Set.Ico s t
  have hRep : processFunction difference.process =
      cell.indicator (processFunction eta.process) := by
    funext z
    change (if z.2 < t then eta.process z.2 z.1 else 0) -
        (if z.2 < s then eta.process z.2 z.1 else 0) = _
    by_cases hs : z.2 < s
    · simp [cell, hs, hs.trans_le hst, not_le.mpr hs]
    · by_cases ht : z.2 < t
      · simp [cell, hs, ht, le_of_not_gt hs, processFunction]
      · simp [cell, hs, ht]
  have hSq : (fun z => (processFunction difference.process z)^2) =
      cell.indicator (fun z => (processFunction eta.process z)^2) := by
    funext z
    rw [hRep]
    by_cases hz : z ∈ cell <;> simp [hz]
  calc
    _ = ∫ omega, (L omega)^2 ∂mu :=
      integral_congr_ae (hInc.mono fun _ h => congrArg (· ^ (2 : ℕ)) h)
    _ = ‖L‖^2 := by
      have h := norm_sq_toLp_eq_integral_sq (Lp.memLp L)
      rw [Lp.toLp_coeFn] at h
      exact h.symm
    _ = ‖integrandToLp difference hB‖^2 := by
      rw [show ‖L‖ = ‖integrandToLp difference hB‖ from itoIntegralTerminal_norm difference hT hB]
    _ = ∫ z, (processFunction difference.process z)^2 ∂(processTimeMeasure mu T) :=
      norm_sq_toLp_eq_integral_sq difference.memLp
    _ = _ := by
      rw [hSq, integral_indicator (measurable_snd measurableSet_Ico)]

#print axioms itoIntegralProcess_increment_isometry

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoIntegralIncrement

steps.title: Use the two terminal representations
steps.text: At each endpoint the actual completed process is the terminal integral of the endpoint-restricted integrand. Linearity puts the increment in L².
steps.lean:
intro increment
  let right := eta.restrictAt t
  let left := eta.restrictAt s
  let difference := ProgressiveL2Algebra.sub right left
  let L := itoIntegralTerminal difference hT hB
  have hL : L = itoIntegralTerminal right hT hB - itoIntegralTerminal left hT hB :=
    itoIntegralTerminal_sub right left hT hB
  have hCoe := Lp.coeFn_sub (itoIntegralTerminal right hT hB) (itoIntegralTerminal left hT hB)
  have hInc : increment =ᵐ[mu] fun omega => L omega := by
    rw [hL]
    filter_upwards [itoIntegralProcess_at_eq_terminal eta hT hB hUsual htT,
      itoIntegralProcess_at_eq_terminal eta hT hB hUsual (hst.trans htT),hCoe] with omega hRt hLt hSub
    exact (congrArg₂ (· - ·) hRt hLt).trans hSub.symm

steps.title: Identify the restricted process
steps.text: The two restrictions agree before s and after t. Their difference on the intervening cell is the original integrand.
steps.lean:
refine ⟨(memLp_congr_ae hInc).2 (Lp.memLp L), ?_⟩
  let cell : Set (Omega × ℝ≥0) := Prod.snd ⁻¹' Set.Ico s t
  have hRep : processFunction difference.process =
      cell.indicator (processFunction eta.process) := by
    funext z
    change (if z.2 < t then eta.process z.2 z.1 else 0) -
        (if z.2 < s then eta.process z.2 z.1 else 0) = _
    by_cases hs : z.2 < s
    · simp [cell, hs, hs.trans_le hst, not_le.mpr hs]
    · by_cases ht : z.2 < t
      · simp [cell, hs, ht, le_of_not_gt hs, processFunction]
      · simp [cell, hs, ht]
  have hSq : (fun z => (processFunction difference.process z)^2) =
      cell.indicator (fun z => (processFunction eta.process z)^2) := by
    funext z
    rw [hRep]
    by_cases hz : z ∈ cell <;> simp [hz]

steps.title: Apply the completed isometry
steps.text: The terminal map preserves the L² norm. The square of the indicator-restricted function integrates over the same cell.
steps.lean:
calc
    _ = ∫ omega, (L omega)^2 ∂mu :=
      integral_congr_ae (hInc.mono fun _ h => congrArg (· ^ (2 : ℕ)) h)
    _ = ‖L‖^2 := by
      have h := norm_sq_toLp_eq_integral_sq (Lp.memLp L)
      rw [Lp.toLp_coeFn] at h
      exact h.symm
    _ = ‖integrandToLp difference hB‖^2 := by
      rw [show ‖L‖ = ‖integrandToLp difference hB‖ from itoIntegralTerminal_norm difference hT hB]
    _ = ∫ z, (processFunction difference.process z)^2 ∂(processTimeMeasure mu T) :=
      norm_sq_toLp_eq_integral_sq difference.memLp
    _ = _ := by
      rw [hSq, integral_indicator (measurable_snd measurableSet_Ico)]
